Maple Avenue Barber Shop

Graphics layer specimen s3.1

Graphics layer

Every mark below is hand-drawn in this repository — inline SVG and CSS, no icon set bought, borrowed or scraped, no font service, no CDN. Nothing on this page loads a file from anywhere but this folder.

Internal specimen. This page exists so the layer can be judged on a phone before any demo is wired to it. It is not a demo, it is not published, and no demo page carries these marks yet.

Icons at both sizes, on all three surfaces

Each icon sits beside its own name: the drawing is decoration and the label carries the meaning, so nothing on a page depends on a glyph being understood. The same set is drawn on paper, on the warm secondary surface and on the ink surface — the stroke is currentColor, so the mark follows whatever surface it is on instead of carrying a colour of its own.

What each mark is for

servicesThe services list and each recorded service card
hours`Opening hours` — also the hours row of the home page
phoneThe printed phone number and the hero's `Call …` button
pinThe recorded address
directions`Get directions`, the link out to a map the visitor already uses
messageThe contact page's message form and the CTA band
emailThe printed email address in the contact fallback
appointmentThe demonstration booking link — a date is asked for, never promised
infoAbout, and the record's own `Good to know` extras
galleryThe Gallery module in the module map
linkThe Socials module in the module map — a link out, not a network's logo
open-externalAny link that leaves our own page, beside the `↗` the template already prints
privacyThe privacy notice link in the footer's small print
arrow-rightA quiet link onward — `More about {name}`

Section grounds

What a section carries when there is no photograph clean enough to use, and the quiet texture a section gets when it needs to read as a different surface. All five are CSS gradients — no image, no file, no request — and they draw in currentColor, so the same ground is a warm hairline on paper and white on ink.

rules Ruled paper — a short list or an hours block
grid A fine grid — a dense section without a photo
arcs Shallow arcs — the scallop the divider family repeats
stripe A 9px diagonal hairline — the quietest ground
no-photo The no-photograph fallback: ink ground, arcs at low contrast, accent hairline on top

A ground on paper, in context

Opening hours

A ruled ground sits behind a short list without becoming a table nobody asked for.

The same ground over ink

The no-photograph hero

When a bundle has no usable photograph, the first screen is an ink ground with arcs and one accent hairline — never a gradient pretending to be a picture.

Dividers

One arc, the same arc doubled, a three-rule stripe and a hairline broken by an accent mark. Each stretches to the width it is given while its stroke stays 1px, so a divider does not get heavier on a wide screen.

arc One shallow arc, 24px — the section break for a photograph-heavy page
arc-pair The same arc doubled — a slower break, for the end of a long section
stripe Three hairlines, the middle one accent — the loudest divider we ship
tick-rule A hairline broken by an accent mark — the page's own eyebrow tick, wider

The schematic map

A stand-in for the map a visitor would open, and plainly not that map: a street plan with no street name, no compass, no scale and no coordinates in it. A demo cannot honestly place a marker — a fictional fixture's address is invented, and a real record's coordinates are not something the record carries — so the drawing carries no geography and its caption does the talking.

The wordmark

The name set in the display face, with a short accent rule under it — and, optionally, the initials mark on the category accent, the same mark the favicon uses. The initials come from the record's own name and nothing is invented; there is no logo, because a business's own mark is the one thing we may never draw.

Name, accent rule, mark — 28px mark, as a header would set it Maple Avenue Barber Shop Name and rule only, where a mark would be a second copy of the same idea Maple Avenue Barber Shop
The same lockup on the ink surface Maple Avenue Barber Shop The mark alone, at 40px

What the layer costs

Measured from the layer's own output, byte for byte. It adds no file and no request to a bundle: the marks are inline markup and the stylesheet is already fetched. The caps are the build's own refusal limits — graphicsProblems() fails a demo build that writes more.

Files this page loads from anywhere but this folder: none. Requests it makes to another origin: none. Icons: 14. Dividers: 4. Grounds: 5. The layer's parts: 6. The page carries no <script> at all, so it renders identically with scripting off; its only files are the two fonts beside it, which every demo already ships.
